questions.q: What is a Microsoft Entra ID Conditional Access policy, in plain terms?
options: An if-this-then-that rule: conditions about a sign-in trigger specific controls
A one-time setup wizard that disables MFA permanently
A static list of blocked IP addresses with no other logic
A feature only available for on-prem Active Directory
questions.explain: Conditional Access evaluates signals (conditions) about a sign-in and applies a response (controls) only when those conditions match.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the signals a Conditional Access policy can evaluate?
options: The user's favorite color, stored as a custom attribute
Who is signing in (user or group)
Where the sign-in is coming from (a named location)
Whether the device is compliant/managed
questions.explain: Real Conditional Access signals include user/group, location, device compliance, and application — not arbitrary custom attributes like favorite color.

questions.q: Entra ID's Security defaults / tenant-wide MFA requirement has what limitation that Conditional Access addresses?
options: It applies the same MFA requirement to every sign-in regardless of risk or context
It only works for Microsoft 365 groups, never security groups
It cannot be enabled for any tenant
It requires a hardware security key for every user
questions.explain: Security defaults are blunt — always-on MFA for everyone. Conditional Access adds adaptive, condition-based logic on top of that.

questions.q: Which license is required to create Conditional Access policies?
options: Microsoft Entra ID P1 (P2 adds risk-based signals)
Microsoft 365 E1 only
No license is required — it's free for every tenant
Azure Reader role
questions.explain: Conditional Access is a premium Entra ID feature that requires at least a P1 license, as introduced back in Lesson 6.

questions.q: In the example policy — Finance group AND sign-in outside the corporate named location THEN require MFA — what happens to a Finance analyst signing in from the office network?
options: They sign in with just their password, since the location condition isn't met
They are always blocked, regardless of location
They must always use a hardware key, never MFA
The policy deletes their account
questions.explain: The MFA control only fires when both conditions match; from the corporate network, the location condition doesn't trigger it.
